operation: OMNI-PAGE-PERSONALITY (each page / main-menu item wears its own identity on the premium floor)
ask: Each page or main-menu item must have their own personalities while serving premium-level surfaces, layouts, everything about UI/UX.
method: 2 parallel read-only Explore agents (identity-mechanism map + top-level page differentiation) then hand-verification of every load-bearing link in the personality pipeline before any change.
key_finding: The platform already has TWO fully-built page-personality systems, but the premium chrome consumes neither — which is the precise cause of the 'samey' look the differentiation agent flagged.

system_a.vocabulary: 11 role/surface slugs (control-plane, tenant-admin, parent, student, teacher, marketing, finance, reports, settings, auth, default)
system_a.resolver: apps/siteconfig/page_personality.py (URL-prefix table -> slug; per-view override; host-kind fallback; operator JSON override CSS)
system_a.emission: UNIVERSAL + server-side — context processors registered in config/settings.py:452-453; data-rmc-page-personality set on <body> in all 5 shells (base, portal_base, marketing, control_plane_skeleton, admin)
system_a.tokens: design-tokens-personality.css — 11 personalities x {accent, soft, tint, strong, deep, on, gradient, eyebrow, glow-rgb}, theme-aware (light+dark), aesthetic-profile + print variants
system_a.consumption_before: only 3 CSS files (rmc-operational-center-frame, rmc-platform-inner-pages, rmc-data-viz) — the accent was computed on every page but the chrome ignored it

system_b.vocabulary: 12 functional-area domains (academic, finance, people, operations, admissions, comms, fleet, hostel, marketplace, security, admin) + per-domain glyph + tagline
system_b.tokens_and_bindings: rmc-page-personality.css — rich component bindings: accent stripe, hero eyebrow glyph, copilot title/tab accent, current-nav accent, focus rings, domain eyebrow chip, per-domain card left-border, hover-inspector
system_b.emission: RARE — only when a template includes partials/rmc_page_personality.html with domain=; otherwise JS-inferred by admin-quickaction.js from the URL (flash; mostly control-plane). So most of the rich bindings never activate.
system_b.verdict: beautiful binding layer that is largely dead because the attribute is seldom emitted server-side

page_header_diagnosis: The shared page header used by ~250 templates (templates/components/page_header.html 126x + templates/studio_os/components/page_header.html 124x) wore NEITHER personality: .rmc-page-eyebrow and .eyebrow were flat gray (--text-tertiary / --admin-content-text-muted) and .rmc-page-header-glow followed tenant --brand-primary only. The identity data was in the DOM on every page; the chrome did not read it.

applied.change: color: var(--text-tertiary,...) -> var(--personality-eyebrow, var(--text-tertiary,...)). The eyebrow on all 124 Studio OS page headers now wears its surface accent (finance green, reports slate, parent amber, teacher blue, student emerald, ...).
applied.risk: low — additive var() with the original as fallback; theme-aware; dark glow header keeps its existing #c7d2fe eyebrow override.

applied.change: color: var(--admin-content-text-muted) -> var(--personality-eyebrow, var(--admin-content-text-muted)). Covers the generic page_header partial (126 templates) + every other .eyebrow site.
applied.risk: low — additive var() fallback chain; no hex added.

applied.change: Added border-inline-start: 3px solid var(--personality-accent, var(--brand-primary, #4f46e5)) — a personality 'spine' on the premium hero header's start edge while the radial glow above stays tenant-brand. Two concerns kept separate: tenant brand = the wash, page personality = the spine + eyebrow.
applied.risk: low — +2px start inset; overridden (intentionally) by the existing --dark variant's border-color on manager dark headers.

applied.change: Bridged System B defaults to System A: --rmc-page-accent / --rmc-page-accent-soft now fall back to the universally-present --personality-accent / -soft (was fixed indigo). Lights up the opt-in accent stripe / eyebrow chip / hover-inspector with the page's surface accent everywhere; explicit [data-rmc-page-domain] still overrides.
applied.risk: low — only affects markup that already opts into those System B components; hex retained as no-personality fallback.

validation.scan_undefined_css_classes: only the 11 pre-existing cockpit-ticker / incident-banner classes from the other in-progress wave (not this wave)
validation.scope: CSS-only wave — no Python / template / migration changes; no Django check or migration-drift run required.

flagged_next_owner_or_per_page.finding: Two parallel personality systems (A role/surface universal-but-unconsumed; B functional-area rich-but-rarely-emitted). Full unification would emit data-rmc-page-domain server-side from a resolver so System B's gated bindings (nav-active accent, hero glyph, focus rings) activate universally without JS/flash.
flagged_next_owner_or_per_page.blocker: the two vocabularies don't map 1:1 (A has reports/auth/parent/student/teacher; B has academic/people/comms/fleet/hostel/marketplace/security). A clean server-side domain resolver needs an owner decision on the canonical per-URL domain map. This wave bridges the un-gated System B components to System A so the gap is materially closed without guessing the mapping.

flagged_next_owner_or_per_page.finding: Genuinely-generic destination pages still read as 'header + table' vs the bespoke dashboards (teacher/student/finance/analytics/founder). Highest-value retrofits: templates/communication/group_list.html, templates/people/backend_{student,teacher,classroom,applicant}_list.html, templates/siteconfig/dashboard_hub.html.
flagged_next_owner_or_per_page.recommendation: Per-page: add a stat ribbon + hero using the SAME proven components (operational-center-frame / decision-engine-surface / rmc-stat-card) the bespoke dashboards use. Per-page because each list's data + card markup differ — a screenshot-diff enhancement wave, not a blind sweep.

principle: The personality pipeline was already plumbed to every page; the missing link was the shared premium chrome reading it. Four additive, theme-aware var() bindings make ~250 page headers + the opt-in accent components wear their surface identity at once — consistent component grammar (the premium floor) + distinct per-page personality (the accent), with zero template churn. The deeper system-unification and per-page bespoke heroes are surfaced with their precise levers rather than guessed.
